'''Mikal Bridges''' (born August 30, 1996) is an American basketball player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova Wildcats]]. He won national championships with Villanova in 2016 and 2018.

==High school career==
Bridges attended Great Valley High School in [[Malvern, Pennsylvania]], where he was coached by Jim Nolan.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Toohey|first1=Terry|title=Bridges stood tall when Villanova needed him most|url=http://www.delcotimes.com/sports/20170316/bridges-stood-tall-when-villanova-needed-him-most|accessdate=July 6, 2017|work=[[Delaware County Daily Times]]|date=March 16, 2017}}</ref> He began to get serious about basketball in his sophomore year, when he had a growth spurt to reach 6-6.<ref name=success/> As a junior, he averaged 20 points and eight rebounds per game. During his senior season, he was named First Team All Class AAAA. He posted averages of 18.5 points, 7.2 rebounds, 2.4 assists, 2.4 blocks and 1.6 steals per game as a senior. Bridges was named to the [[Philadelphia Inquirer]]'s All-Southeastern Pa., boys basketball first team as a senior. In his career, he had 1,340 points and 511 rebounds. Coming out of high school, he was ranked by [[ESPNU]] as the 82nd best player nationally, and committed to Villanova in June 2013.<ref name=villanova>{{Cite web|url=http://www.villanova.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/mikal_bridges_919017.html|title=Mikal Bridges Bio|website=[[Villanova Wildcats]]|access-date=April 12, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://247sports.com/player/mikal-bridges-30556|title=Mikal Bridges, Villanova Wildcats, Small Forward|website=247Sports|access-date=April 12, 2016}}</ref>

==College career==
=== Freshman ===
Bridges redshirted his freshman season and assisted in scouting players.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Frank|first1=Reuben|title=NCAA Tournament: Mikal Bridges, from redshirt to 'vital part'|url=http://www.csnphilly.com/ncaa/ncaa-tournament-mikal-bridges-redshirt-vital-part|accessdate=July 5, 2017|work=CSN Philly|date=March 16, 2016}}</ref> In Bridges's first year with [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]] he appeared in all 40 games for the Wildcats. He said he had to do a lot of lifting weights and changing his three point shot.<ref name="everything"/> He had a key role coming off the bench in the [[2016 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2016 NCAA Tournament]], scoring 11 points in a [[Final Four]] rout of the [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma Sooners]]. Bridges won the NCAA championship along with his teammates for the school for the first time since 1985. He averaged 6.4 points, 3.2 rebounds and 1.1 steals per game as a freshman.<ref name=villanova/> "He came in as a high school scoring phenom like they all do, so I'm really proud of how he has opened up his game defensively," coach [[Jay Wright (basketball)|Jay Wright]] said.<ref name="specialist">{{cite news|last1=Frank|first1=Reuben|title=For Villanova, Mikal Bridges Has Become A Defensive Specialist|url=http://www.csnphilly.com/villanova-wildcats/villanova-mikal-bridges-has-become-defensive-specialist|accessdate=July 5, 2017|work=CSN Philly|date=March 14, 2017}}</ref>

=== Sophomore ===
[[File:20170213 Villanova-Depaul Mikal Bridges dunk.jpg|thumb|Left|Bridges dunking against DePaul in 2017]]
Coming into the 2016-17 season, Bridges was slated to be the team's sixth man but started every game after [[Phil Booth (basketball)|Phil Booth]] went down with a knee injury in November. As a sophomore, Joe Juliano of ''[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]'' wrote, "If there is such a thing as a five-tool player in college basketball, Mikal Bridges is the model."<ref name="everything">{{cite news|last1=Juliano|first1=Joe|title=Mikal Bridges doing a little bit of everything for Villanova|url=http://www.philly.com/philly/sports/colleges/villanova/20170307_Mikal_Bridges_doing_a_little_bit_of_everything_for_Villanova.html|accessdate=July 5, 2017|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|date=March 6, 2017}}</ref> He became well-regarded as a lanky forward who could score and play excellent defense and often guarded the opposing team's best player.<ref name="specialist"/> In the NCAA Tournament, he scored 13 points to help Villanova to a first round victory over [[Mount St. Mary's Mountaineers men's basketball|Mount St. Mary's]]. Bridges averaged 9.8 points and 4.6 rebounds per game while making 54 percent of his field goal attempts and 39 percent of three point tries.<ref name=villanova/> He improved his scoring as the season progressed, averaging 12.3 points in his last 12 games of the regular season. Along with Creighton's Khyri Thomas and teammate [[Josh Hart (basketball)|Josh Hart]], Bridges was one of three Big East defensive player of the year honorees, being third in the conference in steals with 1.9 per game.<ref name="everything"/>

Again|url=http://www.bigeast.com/news/2017/10/18/mens-basketball-villanova-viewed-as-league-favorite-again.aspx|accessdate=October 27, 2017|date=October 18, 2017|publisher=[[Big East Conference]]|website=BigEast.com}}</ref> Bridges hit all six 3-point tries in a 24-point performance against [[Lafayette Leopards men's basketball|Lafayette]] on November 17.<ref>{{cite 2018|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=November 17, 2017}}</ref> On December 4, Bridges scored a career-high 28 points to go with six rebounds and two blocks in an 88-72 victory over [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Stubbs|first1=Roman|title=Villanova’s Mikal Bridges puts on a show at Madison Square unanimous Big East first team|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2018/03/04/bluiett-brunson-martin-unanimous-big-east-first-team/111086824/|accessdate=March 31, 2018|work=[[USA 2018|work=[[Philadelphia Inquirer]]|date=March 10, 2018}}</ref>

On April 10, 2018, Bridges announced his intention to forgo his final season of collegiate eligibility and declare for the [[2018 NBA Draft]], where he is expected to be a first round selection.<ref>{{Cite news|first=Adrian |last=Wojnarowski|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/23099657/villanova-wildcats-all-america-forward-mikal-bridges-bypass-senior-season-enter-nba-draft|title=Villanova's Mikal Bridges to bypass final season, enter NBA draft|work=[[ESPN]]|access-date= April 10, 2018|date=April 10, 2018}}</ref>
